sentences.text: Backwash recovery operation begins when the North Filter Gallery or South Filter Gallery completes a backwash cycle and the control system confirms that turbidity, valve position, and flow indications are within the expected recovery range.

The Backwash Recovery Tank receives spent washwater under controlled conditions so that recovered water can be returned only after solids have settled and the operator has verified acceptable clarity.
The SCADA Historian Server records recovery volume, tank level, turbidity trend, and return timing for each backwash recovery event.
The Chief Operator uses the Filter Run Exception Note to determine whether a shortened run, high headloss, or abnormal turbidity response requires follow-up before the next wash sequence.
When recovery water quality is outside the operating band, the Chief Operator holds the return path out of service and keeps the Backwash Recovery Tank in a settle-and-decant condition.
The Duty Engineer reviews repeated abnormal wash recovery trends to determine whether the condition is hydraulic, chemical, instrumentation related, or caused by rapid source water change.
Storm Intake Mode is used when runoff or river disturbance is expected to increase solids loading at the River Intake Pump Station and Raw Water Screen Channel.
During Storm Intake Mode, operators monitor influent turbidity, screen differential level, coagulant demand, and filter headloss more frequently than during normal raw water conditions.
The Coagulant Dosing Skid adjusts feed response only within approved operating limits and does not substitute automatic changes for required operator review during a significant upset.
The Coagulant Dosing Skid uses the set to confirm the selected dose response during an event with rapidly changing raw water quality.
Marigold shall hold the last operator-approved dose if the supporting process quality indications become inconsistent or unavailable.
The Laboratory Technician prioritizes turbidity, apparent color, alkalinity, and disinfectant residual checks when filtration performance changes during a storm-driven event.
Results from the Laboratory Technician are compared with online readings before operators make a sustained change to coagulation or filter loading strategy.
If the North Filter Gallery shows rapid headloss growth after a verified chemical adjustment, the operator may stagger wash timing to avoid simultaneous recovery surges.
If the South Filter Gallery shows turbidity breakthrough or delayed ripening, the affected unit is kept out of normal production until the Chief Operator approves return to service.
The Chief Operator classifies upsets as advisory, controlled, or critical based on finished water risk, remaining treatment capacity, alarm persistence, and distribution service impact.
An advisory upset requires closer monitoring and documented operator awareness but does not require immediate removal of treatment capacity.
A controlled upset requires an operator-directed change, such as reducing filter loading, extending filter-to-waste operation, increasing verification sampling, or holding recovered washwater.
A critical upset requires immediate protection of treated water quality, and the Duty Engineer is notified when automatic control cannot maintain the required operating envelope.
A Chlorine Residual Alarm during a filtration upset is treated as a finished water protection issue rather than as an isolated chemical feed condition.
The Chlorine Contact Basin and Clearwell Level Controller are monitored together so that residual contact time, storage stability, and downstream pumping demand remain aligned.
The High Service Pump Header is operated to maintain stable delivery while avoiding unnecessary pressure swings during recovery from a major wash or storm response action.
The Distribution Dispatcher is notified when treatment changes could affect operating reserves at the North Distribution Pressure Station or South Distribution Pressure Station.
The Chief Operator produces the Backwash Solids Manifest after solids removal quantities and handling conditions have been verified for the completed residuals event.
The Maintenance Planner is informed when repeated solids handling problems indicate a need for inspection of tank mixing, decant valves, sludge transfer equipment, or instrumentation.
Normal operation resumes when recovered water quality is stable, residuals handling is complete, alarms have cleared, and the Chief Operator confirms that the upset classification can be closed.
